articles.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
articles.summary: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters. The lawsuit claims the […]

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.summary: Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary: Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

articles.title: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.

articles.title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need
articles.summary: Founded in February, Humyn Labs competes with startups including Mecka AI and XDOF, with about 90% of its revenue coming from the U.S.

articles.title: Anthropic set to price IPO in key test for AI boom
articles.summary: Anthropic prices its blockbuster IPO on Wednesday, giving ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant in a test of how long the artificial intelligence spending boom can last.

articles.title: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
articles.summary: Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called "Visuals," allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork. Visuals […]

articles.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
articles.summary: Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content - including, as of late, from one of Meta's most prominent executives. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and […]

articles.title: The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed
articles.summary: The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year. "While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address […]

articles.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. At the […]

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.

articles.title: Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain
articles.summary: Scientists have filmed tiny magnetic vortices called skyrmions melting out of an organized lattice for the first time, revealing new ways to manipulate these unusual structures. The breakthrough could help make brain-like computers a reality, potentially enabling dramatically smaller and more energy-efficient technology.

articles.title: Researchers find eight ways AI could lead to our downfall
articles.summary: Government and academic assessments, including reports from the U.K. Government Office for Science and the RAND Corporation, have not ruled out the possibility that AI could lead to human extinction or societal collapse. To protect against such severe risks, we must first understand how those risks could unfold.

articles.title: Robots learn human movement patterns to find paths through dense crowds
articles.summary: Navigating a bustling train station or airport is a major challenge for people with visual impairments. New research from Örebro University teaches robots to follow the "unwritten rules" of human movement and make their way through dense crowds. In the long term, the technology could serve as a digital complement to guide dogs.

articles.title: Chinese robots learn from humans in tech hub Shenzhen
articles.summary: At a park refreshment stand in China's tech capital, Shenzhen, a humanoid robot grabs a cup and pulls a lever to form an ice cream spiral, then hands the customer their order.

articles.title: After a 13-year wait, 'Grand Theft Auto VI' arrives with enormous hype and expectations
articles.summary: After a 13-year wait, one of entertainment's biggest releases is finally here.

articles.title: Cambridge Dictionary chooses 'human' as word of the year in response to AI fears
articles.summary: Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist.

articles.title: Waymo suspends all driverless taxi rides on freeways after ban in California
articles.summary: Waymo has temporarily stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from state freeways following recent traffic incidents.

articles.title: Classified communications network at the National Security Agency goes down, defense official says
articles.summary: An internal network the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline Tuesday after what the agency described as "routine maintenance."

articles.title: FAA halts installation of routers that led to ground stop
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration announced on Tuesday that it was pausing the installation of the routers that were linked to last week's national ground stop and turned off any Juniper routers that were already installed.

articles.title: Apple joins a parade of technology hiccups in recent days
articles.summary: An update gone awry Tuesday at Apple followed a rash of major outages in recent days, including problems affecting the Federal Aviation Administration, United Airlines and Microsoft.
